document.title: Experiment is live but shows 0 exposures / data in UI

results.title: Experiment is live but shows 0 exposures / data in UI

snippets.text: We launched a new experiment yesterday and the Results page still shows 0 exposures and no metric conversions. The flag was previously used in another experiment. Snowflake shows reason_detail 'inExperiment = true' but the experiment iteration ID is blank, and Live Events show stale flag versions.
Engineering confirmed this is a bug — a regression introduced in a recent update to experimentation functionality. The identical experiment setup worked correctly in staging.

results.title: 0 exposure for experiment — flag is in experiment but getting 0 exposure

snippets.text: Created this experiment and it has 0 exposure. Are you seeing feature events for this flag in Live events, and does the event detail show inExperiment: true? Likely the SDK isn't sending experiment events — possibly page redirects after variation() without an explicit flush().

document.title: Troubleshooting experimentation metrics from Segment (Twilio) not registering conversions

results.title: Troubleshooting experimentation metrics from Segment (Twilio) not registering conversions

snippets.text: The context is successfully evaluated by the experimentation flag and metric events are visible in the UI, but conversion counts are not reflected in the experiment results. Common cause: mismatch in randomization unit between the experiment and the metric, or incorrect Segment destination mapping for the context kind.

document.title: Error 'This metric has never received an event for this iteration'

results.title: Error 'This metric has never received an event for this iteration'

snippets.text: After starting an iteration the Results page shows 'This metric has never received an event for this iteration.' LaunchDarkly has not received a metric event with a context key matching a feature event. If using a JavaScript SDK, ad-blockers or Do Not Track can block the events needed to register the metric.

The health error 'Sample mismatch ratio detected. These results are not valid.' means LaunchDarkly detected a mismatch between audience allocation and observed exposures. Most commonly the randomization method is incorrect, or a shared anonymous context key causes multiple users to be treated as a single context, skewing variation exposure.

document.title: Sample Ratio Mismatch — Root Causes, Frequency, and Diagnostic Tiers

results.title: Sample Ratio Mismatch — Root Causes, Frequency, and Diagnostic Tiers

snippets.text: ~50% of SRM escalations are Tier 1 (data already in LD, just not surfaced in the UI). Self Financial: experiments starting 90/10 then restarted 50/50 show a big bias toward control that takes a long time to converge. Customer using Fastly edge bucketed users into variants too early, causing SRM.

Active SRM subthemes in customer feedback: 'Persistent Sample Ratio Mismatch Warnings', 'SRM Persists Across Unchanged Iterations', 'General Help With SRM', and 'Add Exposure Imbalance Notifications' (improvement request). Genuine Parts / Motion: persistent SRM across many experiments, unresolved.

Top pain points: provide experiment analysis enablement (86), expand data warehouse coverage (59), difficulty diagnosing persistent sample ratio mismatch (34), data integrity issues skew results (32). 7 of the top 10 pain points cluster in Stage 5 (Experiments).

We are losing about 50% of our experiment data by the time it reaches Databricks — a custom backend identifier (application_id) is missing from exported contexts, so we cannot join LaunchDarkly data with our internal datasets.

The customer can make only one variation call and is trying to solve a multi-flag setup with one experiment call — wants to fetch a parent feature flag and based on that make multiple calls. The platform limitation is that you can only attach an experiment to one flag at a time; parent/child flag relationships don't return child variations.

Before-and-after analysis is the biggest challenge in experimentation for this customer. They want to attach metrics that LaunchDarkly automatically monitors as part of a guarded release — checkout percentage, page load time — but are unsure how to wire warehouse metrics into the analysis.

document.title: Blitz: Snowflake Warehouse Native Experimentation Setup Overhaul

results.title: Blitz: Snowflake Warehouse Native Experimentation Setup Overhaul

snippets.text: The old Snowflake Warehouse Native Experimentation setup required customers to bounce between 3 interfaces — the LD UI, the Snowflake Marketplace, and a Snowflake Worksheet — installing a native app that added no real value. Customers found it confusing that an environment without Data Export configured silently does not show up in the dropdown.
